deciding_assertions: partition_stats_exactness.test: after 'DELETE FROM big WHERE id = 0' (committed, same process) and again after CHECKPOINT, EXPLAIN SELECT count(*) must NOT contain 'Sequential Scan'; also after the first CHECKPOINT (version info still loaded, no deletes) EXPLAIN SELECT min(id), max(id) must not contain 'Sequential Scan'
reason: The issue scopes the bug to tables with no deletion and asks only about count. The narrowest reasonable fix treats loaded version info with no deletes (and no uncommitted changes) as an exact count; it passes the append-only count assertions but leaves count approximate after a committed DELETE, so it fails the two 'count after in-process delete is folded' assertions. A fix that changes only the count exactness also fails the min/max-after-checkpoint assertion, which the issue never mentions.

deciding_assertions: timestamp_casts.test: the 9-column query needs TRY_CAST(TIMESTAMP 'infinity' AS TIME), AS TIMETZ, TRY_CAST(TIMESTAMPTZ 'infinity' AS TIMETZ), TRY_CAST('infinity'::TIMESTAMP_NS AS TIME / TIME_NS), TRY_CAST('infinity'::TIMESTAMPTZ_NS AS TIMETZ) all IS NULL (plus statement errors 'Can't get TIME of infinite TIMESTAMP' for CAST)
reason: The issue shows one failure: TRY_CAST of an out-of-range TIMESTAMP to TIMESTAMP_NS throws the precision error. A reasonable fix makes the timestamp precision-conversion casts (TIMESTAMP, TIMESTAMPTZ, TIMESTAMP_MS, TIMESTAMP_S to the NS types) honour TRY_CAST; it passes the issue case and its direct variants but not the infinite-timestamp to TIME/TIMETZ/TIME_NS casts, which are a different cast and failure mode that the issue does not state. The broad title ('Time-related type') leaves some room, so confidence is medium.

deciding_assertions: interval_row_group_pruning.test: count(*) WHERE iv > INTERVAL '5000 days' = 1143; EXPLAIN ANALYZE on the reattached v2.0.0 file shows 'Row Groups Scanned: 1 / 3'; the v1.5.3 compat file still returns 1143
reason: A reasonable fix adds min/max statistics for INTERVAL columns and lets the normalized_interval(iv) > constant filter use them; adding INTERVAL to the numeric statistics forces serialization support, so stats survive detach/reattach and pruning gives exactly 1 of 3 row groups (only the last one holds values above 5000 days). The counts are plain correctness values; the compat part only asserts the count, which any fix that writes or omits interval stats passes.

deciding_assertions: bloom_filters.test: 'Row Groups Scanned: 0 / 10' for list_value[1] = 101, list_extract(list_value, 1) = 101 and deep_list[1][1][1] = 101; counts 0, and no wrong pruning for deep_list[1][1][1] = 100 (205) and list_value[2] = 102 (205)
reason: The issue asks that equality filters on elements of a Parquet LIST column check the leaf bloom filter, and its own repro data includes the triple-nested deep_list column. A reasonable fix maps array_extract/list_extract (same operation, alias entry point) down to the primitive leaf, also through nested lists, and prunes all 10 row groups; the remaining assertions only check that matching values are not pruned. Medium because a fix that handles only one list level would fail the deep_list assertion, although the issue's data names that column.

deciding_assertions: bloom_filter_interval.test: parquet_kv_metadata(...) WHERE key = 'duckdb.interval_bloom_filter' AND decode(value) = 'normalized-v1' must return 1 for both written files
reason: The issue only asks that the Parquet reader prune row groups for an INTERVAL equality filter. The test requires the writer to emit a new key-value metadata entry with the exact key 'duckdb.interval_bloom_filter' and value 'normalized-v1', names that the real fix invents and the issue never gives. A reasonable fix (for example, hashing normalized intervals in the bloom filter and checking it on read) can prune 0 of 10 row groups and still fails these assertions.

deciding_assertions: plaintext_footer_encryption.test (the only fail-to-pass test): reading data/parquet-testing/plaintext_footer_crypto_metadata.parquet must fail with 'Invalid Input Error: File is encrypted but no file crypto metadata is set'
reason: The issue is about an encrypted file that can be read without a key when parquet_metadata_cache is on. The graded test instead reads a plaintext-footer encrypted file with no metadata cache involved and expects a new exact error message that the real fix adds in the column reader. A reasonable fix that validates the encryption config on cache hits does not touch this path and fails the assertion; the issue-related checks in parquet_encryption.test are not in either test list.

deciding_assertions: multiple_column_stats_pruning.test: 'Row Groups Scanned: 0 / 4' for i > j, i >= j, i = j, j < i, j <= i (i has NULLs); UNION ALL query keeps a CTE in the optimized plan and still shows 0 / 4; partially_matching table i > j shows 3 / 4 and count 199999
reason: The issue asks that column-to-column predicates use per-row-group min/max stats to skip row groups. A reasonable fix pushes such comparisons into the scan and checks both columns' zonemaps for every comparison operator and either column order (direct variants of the stated predicate type), ignoring NULLs as the existing zonemap checks do; it gives 0/4, and 3/4 where only the first row group lies below j. The CTE assertion only keeps existing common-subplan behaviour. Medium because the operator variants and the CTE guard depend on what counts as a direct variant or existing behaviour.

deciding_assertions: total_string_length_dictionary.test: issue repro (force_compression='dictionary', 10000 x 'hello', CHECKPOINT); storage_info compression = Dictionary (existing behaviour); stats(s).total_string_length = 50000
reason: The test runs the issue's own example and expects the true total of every row (10000 x 5 = 50000; the issue's '5000' is an arithmetic slip, but it clearly asks for repeated strings to be counted). The narrowest reasonable fix, which adds the length of each repeated dictionary lookup to the stats during compression, gives 50000 and does not change the compression choice, so it passes.

deciding_assertions: string_prefix.test: EXPLAIN plans must show 's = ''09999000''' and 'Row Groups Scanned: 1 / 82' for substring(s, 1) = '09999000', substring(s, 1, 9) = '09999000', array_slice(s, 1, 9) = '09999000', s[:] = '09999000'; s[0:5] and s[:5] must give the range filter (s >= '09999') AND (s < '0999:') with 1 / 82
reason: The issue asks only that a prefix extraction compared with a constant of the same length (substring/s[1:5] = '09999') prune like LIKE '09999%'. The narrowest reasonable fix rewrites substring(s, 1, n) = c and s[1:n] = c with length(c) = n to a prefix comparison. It passes those cases. It does not rewrite whole-string extractions or shorter constants into an equality, so the EXPLAIN assertions that expect 's = ...' and 1 / 82 fail. The issue does not mention those cases, nor the 0 and omitted start bounds.

deciding_assertions: substring_zonemap_pruning.test: Row Groups Scanned 1/5 or 2/5 for substr(s, 2, 4) = '4950', s[2:] > ..., s[2:5] > ..., s[:] > ..., s[0:2]/s[1:2]/s[:2] > 'p3', substr(s, 1, 2) > 'p3', substr(s, 0, 3) > 'p3', s[2:20] > ..., and for truncated-stats strings (substr(s, 2) = '495000' || repeat('x', 20)); test_string_util.cpp calls the new StringUtil::GetCommonPrefixSize
reason: The issue shows one case: substr(s, 2) = constant when all values share the removed prefix 'p'. The narrowest reasonable fix derives stats for two-argument substring from min/max with a shared removed prefix. It passes the issue's case. It fails the bracket-slice (array_slice), three-argument, range-comparison, prefix-length and truncated-bound pruning assertions, which the issue never mentions. Also, the C++ unit test added in the same test change calls the new helper StringUtil::GetCommonPrefixSize, which the issue does not give. If that file is compiled into the test binary, the build fails without that exact name.

deciding_assertions: read_json_dates.test: iso8601_mixed_same_field.json (Z value, null, plain value) -> VARCHAR for all rows; iso8601_vector_boundary.json (2048 Z rows then 1 plain) -> VARCHAR; iso8601_mixed_infinity.json -> VARCHAR; read_json_timestamp_specials.test 'True mix remains VARCHAR'
reason: The issue asks that ISO 8601 strings with Z or an offset be inferred as TIMESTAMPTZ. It does not say what a field that mixes offset and plain timestamps should become. The tests require a fallback to VARCHAR. A reasonable fix that keeps the existing TIMESTAMP result for mixed fields, or picks TIMESTAMPTZ when any value has an offset (the issue argues that offsets make TIMESTAMPTZ the safe choice), passes the offset-only cases but fails these mixed-field assertions.

deciding_assertions: trigger_dependency.test and trigger_dependency_restart.test: DROP TABLE log RESTRICT error must match 'trigger "tr" on table "t" depends on table "log"'; CREATE TRIGGER that references temp.log6 must fail with 'cannot reference.*different catalog'; ALTER TABLE t7 RENAME TO fails while ALTER TABLE t7 RENAME COLUMN succeeds; ALTER TABLE t9/src11 RENAME COLUMN fails when the body reads the column; DROP TABLE t2 without CASCADE succeeds
reason: The issue asks only that DROP TABLE log RESTRICT fail while a trigger body references log. The narrowest reasonable fix records the tables that the trigger body references as blocking dependencies. It produces the existing dependency message 'trigger "tr" depends on table "log"', which fails the regex that needs the new 'on table "t"' text. The cross-catalog rejection (a new error) and the specific ALTER rename and column-alter rules are behaviour that the issue never mentions.

deciding_assertions: test_icu_datesub.test: date_sub isoyear/era across 1 BC/1 AD = 1/-1, date_sub('year', 2 BC, 2 AD) = 3, coptic and japanese era date_sub = 1/-1 and 4/-4; test_icu_datediff.test: date_diff isoyear = 2/-2, era = 1/-1, same-era 0, coptic/roc/japanese era date_diff = 1/-1 and 4/-4
reason: The issue says the InternalException should be either 'a normal user-facing error or correct result'. The tests need numeric results. A reasonable fix that turns the ICU failure into a normal user-facing error passes nothing here. The tests also fix era semantics for the coptic, roc and japanese calendars and year arithmetic across BC/AD, which the issue does not state.

deciding_assertions: partition_stats_exactness.test: after 'DELETE FROM big WHERE id = 0' (committed, in process), and again after the following CHECKPOINT, EXPLAIN SELECT count(*) FROM big must NOT contain 'Sequential Scan' (count folded from stats despite deletes); also min/max folded after CHECKPOINT on the append-only table
reason: The issue asks for count(*) to come from stats on tables with no deletion. The narrowest reasonable fix makes the count exact when the loaded version info has no deletes and no uncommitted changes; it passes the append-only assertions but still scans after the committed in-process DELETE, so it fails the two count assertions that expect folding with deletes. Folding counts on tables with deletes is a case the issue excludes by its own title.

deciding_assertions: timestamp_casts.test: TRY_CAST(TIMESTAMP 'infinity' AS TIME), AS TIMETZ, TIMESTAMPTZ 'infinity' AS TIMETZ, TIMESTAMP_NS 'infinity' AS TIME / TIME_NS, TIMESTAMPTZ_NS 'infinity' AS TIMETZ must all be NULL (9-column true row); also CAST of TIMESTAMPTZ_NS to TIMETZ value check
reason: The issue shows one failing TRY_CAST: an out-of-range timestamp to TIMESTAMP_NS (precision increase). The narrowest reasonable fix makes the precision-increase casts (TIMESTAMP, _MS, _S, TZ to _NS) honor TRY_CAST; it passes those assertions but the infinite-timestamp to TIME/TIMETZ/TIME_NS casts still throw, so the combined TRY_CAST row fails. Those casts are a different operation and failure mode, named only by the vague title 'Time-related type'.

deciding_assertions: interval_row_group_pruning.test: after writing with STORAGE_VERSION 'v2.0.0', detach and re-attach, EXPLAIN ANALYZE ... WHERE iv > INTERVAL '5000 days' shows 'Row Groups Scanned: 1 / 3'; counts 1143 for both v2.0.0 and v1.5.3 files
reason: The test is the issue's own query shape (interval column, '>' constant through normalized_interval) on a smaller table. A reasonable fix adds interval min/max statistics, makes the normalized_interval filter usable for zonemap checks, and serializes the new stats like other numeric stats (always, or gated on the existing V2_0_0 version); either variant prunes to 1/3 after reload and keeps counts correct. Only a fix that deliberately never persists interval stats would fail the reload check, which I do not count as the normal design.

deciding_assertions: bloom_filters.test: 'Row Groups Scanned: 0 / 10' for list_value[1] = 101, list_extract(list_value, 1) = 101, and deep_list[1][1][1] = 101; correctness counts 0, 205 (deep_list[1][1][1] = 100), 205 (list_value[2] = 102)
reason: A reasonable fix maps an equality on list element extraction to the list's primitive leaf column and checks its bloom filter. It passes the issue's own query, the list_extract alias (same operation through a second entry point), and the correctness counts. The deep_list column is part of the issue's own repro data, so descending through nested list extractions to the leaf is implied; a one-level-only fix would fail that assertion, hence medium.

deciding_assertions: bloom_filter_interval.test: parquet_kv_metadata must hold key 'duckdb.interval_bloom_filter' with value 'normalized-v1' (count 1) for both the flat and nested files; nested iv_list[1] = ... and iv_struct.iv = ... must prune to 'Row Groups Scanned: 0 / 10'
reason: The issue asks that INTERVAL equality filters prune Parquet row groups via the bloom filter. The test requires a new file key-value marker whose key and value are constants invented by the real fix; a correct fix that writes and checks normalized interval bloom filters without this marker fails both kv_metadata assertions. Nested list and struct interval columns are also not in the issue.

deciding_assertions: plaintext_footer_encryption.test (the only fail_to_pass test): read_parquet of a new plaintext-footer file whose column chunks carry crypto metadata must fail with 'Invalid Input Error: File is encrypted but no file crypto metadata is set'
reason: The issue asks that cached Parquet metadata not let an encrypted file be read without (or with the wrong) key. A reasonable fix validates the key against the cache entry or bypasses cached stats for encrypted files; it does not touch plaintext-footer encrypted files and does not produce this new message, so it fails the only graded test. The parquet_encryption.test changes that cover the issue's case are not in either test list.

deciding_assertions: multiple_column_stats_pruning.test: 'Row Groups Scanned: 0 / 4' for i > j, i >= j, i = j, j < i, j <= i; count 0; UNION ALL of 'i > j AND i >= 0' still becomes a CTE and scans 0 / 4; partially_matching i > j scans 3 / 4 with count 199999
reason: A reasonable fix prunes row groups for column-to-column comparisons using per-row-group min/max of both columns; the other comparison operators and the swapped operand order are direct variants of the issue's i > j, and the 0/4 and 3/4 counts follow from any correct per-row-group pruning. The CTE check only asks that the existing common-subplan detection keep working, which a reasonable fix must preserve. Medium because the '=' operator and the CTE interplay depend on the reading of direct variants and of preservation.

deciding_assertions: total_string_length_dictionary.test: after CHECKPOINT with force_compression='dictionary' (v1.0.0 storage), compression is Dictionary and stats(s).total_string_length = 50000 for 10000 rows of 'hello'
reason: The issue gives the exact repro: dictionary compression counts only unique strings in total_string_length. The narrowest reasonable fix also adds the string length for repeated (already in the dictionary) values during compression, which gives 10000 x 5 = 50000; the issue's '5000' is an arithmetic slip, and any correct per-row count passes. The Dictionary check is existing behaviour under the issue's forced compression.

deciding_assertions: string_prefix.test: substring(s, 1) = '09999000', substring(s, 1, 9) = '09999000', array_slice(s, 1, 9) = '09999000' and s[:] = '09999000' must show plan filter s = '09999000' with Row Groups Scanned 1 / 82; also s[0:5] and s[:5] must become (s >= '09999') AND (s < '0999:')
reason: The issue asks that substring and s[1:5] equality with a constant of the extracted length become a prefix filter. The narrowest reasonable fix rewrites substring(s, 1, n) = c and array_slice(s, 1, n) = c to prefix(s, c) when length(c) = n; it passes those cases but fails the asserted equality rewrites for shorter constants, the two-argument substring(s, 1), and the unbounded s[:] slice, none of which the issue states.

deciding_assertions: substring_zonemap_pruning.test: bracket slices s[2:], s[2:5], s[:], s[0:2], s[:2], s[2:20] must prune (1 / 5 or 2 / 5); substr(s, 0, 3) > 'p3' must scan 2 / 5; substring_truncated_pruning (strings longer than the stored min/max bytes) must scan 1 / 5 for substr(s, 2) and s[2:]
reason: The issue shows only substr(s, 2) = '005000' on short strings that share a one-character prefix. The narrowest reasonable fix adds statistics propagation for substr/substring with a constant positive offset when min and max share the removed prefix, and returns no stats when bounds are truncated or the offset is not positive; it passes the issue's case but fails the array_slice (bracket) tests in the core_functions extension, the offset-0 cases, and the truncated-bounds pruning tests.

deciding_assertions: read_json_dates.test: iso8601_mixed_same_field (Z value, null, plain value in one field) must give VARCHAR; iso8601_vector_boundary (2048 Z rows then 1 plain row) must give VARCHAR; iso8601_mixed_infinity must give VARCHAR; read_json_timestamp_specials.test: infinity/epoch must not count as offset evidence (plain + infinity stays TIMESTAMP, offset + infinity is TIMESTAMPTZ)
reason: The issue asks that ISO 8601 strings with Z or an offset be inferred as TIMESTAMPTZ. The narrowest reasonable fix tries TIMESTAMPTZ first and keeps it only when every value has an offset, else falls back to the existing TIMESTAMP inference; that fix passes the single-value cases but gives TIMESTAMP (or TIMESTAMPTZ) for a field that mixes offset and plain values, while the tests require VARCHAR, a design choice the issue never states, and it also needs special handling of infinity/epoch values.

deciding_assertions: trigger_dependency.test and trigger_dependency_restart.test: DROP TABLE log RESTRICT error must match 'trigger "tr" on table "t" depends on table "log"'; CREATE TRIGGER referencing temp.log6 must fail with 'cannot reference ... different catalog'; ALTER TABLE src11 RENAME COLUMN j TO k and ALTER TABLE t9 RENAME COLUMN j TO k must fail while t7/t10 column alters succeed; DROP TABLE t2 (trigger's own table) must succeed without CASCADE
reason: The issue asks that a table referenced by a trigger body be protected from DROP RESTRICT. The narrowest reasonable fix records the body's catalog entries as normal dependencies of the trigger; DROP RESTRICT then fails with the existing dependency message, which renders the trigger as 'trigger "tr" depends on table "log"' and fails the regex that needs the new 'on table "t"' part. The tests also assert a new cross-catalog error text and fine-grained ALTER blocking rules that the issue does not mention.

deciding_assertions: test_icu_datesub.test: date_sub('isoyear'|'era', '1-01-01 (BC)', '1-01-01') = 1 / -1, date_sub('year', 2 BC, 2 AD) = 3 / -3, era subtraction in coptic (1) and japanese (4) calendars; test_icu_datediff.test: date_diff isoyear across BC/AD = 2 / -2, era = 1 / -1, era in coptic and roc (1) and japanese (4), era added to the TIMESTAMPTZ_NS part loop
reason: The issue says the InternalException should become 'a normal user-facing error or correct result', so it offers two outcomes; a reasonable fix that raises a user-facing error for the BC/AD isoyear case fails every new assertion, which require numeric results. The tests also check era differences in the coptic, roc and japanese calendars and the year part, which the issue does not state.
